svg.text: End-to-End Deep Learning Stack - github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad - UOp IR + lazy fusion + hackable compiler
L1 - Frontend + Workloads (PyTorch-like ergonomics - JAX IR - TVM scheduling - intentionally tiny)
L2 - Tensor to UOp Graph (lazy DAG - canonical IR - entire stack is graph rewrites)
Immutable node: op + dtype + src + arg
base = contiguous compute buffer - view = ShapeTracker view
Tensor ops are syntactic sugar over UOp construction
RESHAPE PERMUTE SHRINK FLIP - zero-copy views
SINK marks end of compute chains for scheduling
Extensibility core - all passes are rewrites
L3 - Scheduling + Memory Planning + JIT (break UOp graph into kernels - LINEAR execution plan)
Split large graph into subgraphs = one GPU kernel
Output: LINEAR UOp w/ CALL list
CALL src[0]=SINK ast - rest are buffer args
Lazy matmul+sum fuses to single kernel
BUFFER UOps tied to device allocators
COPY between devices as schedule ops
Replay compiled kernels on subsequent runs
Symbolic vars for dynamic shape support
MULTI MSELECT MSTACK for sharded tensors
L4 - Rangeify + Compilation Pipeline (lower to loops - optimize - linearize for codegen)
Tensor ops to Ops.RANGE loop vars + Ops.INDEX
UPCAST UNROLL LOCAL TC tensor core opts
DAG to flat instruction stream w/ control flow
Late passes: lower index types - load/store collapse
DEBUG=3 shows fused schedule - DEBUG=4 codegen
UOp viz + process replay kernel diff tests
L5 - Renderer + Code Generation (device-specific source from lowered UOp graph)
Each Ops enum maps to target language expr
PTX - WGSL - LLVM IR - NIR - PythonProgram emu
NVRTC/nvcc for CUDA - MSL for Metal - etc
New accelerator only needs ~25 ops implemented
Hackable backend surface - ops_*.py per device
kernel - copy - view - encdec - graph runners
L6 - Runtime + HCQ Execution (device alloc - launch - async graphs - multi-device sync)
Tensor API - UOp Graph - Schedule - Rangeify - Lowering - Codegen - Execution
Step 1: Lazy Tensor ops build canonical UOp DAG (dedup via UOpMetaClass)
Step 2: Scheduler topo-sort - kernel grouping - memory_plan_rewrite - LINEAR+CALL
Step 3: run_rangeify - RANGE/INDEX loops - movement op lowering - multi_pm split
Step 4: full_rewrite_to_sink - symbolic - BEAM opts - expander - devectorizer - linearize
Step 5: Renderer emits device code - compile - get_runtime - Ops.PROGRAM kernel
Step 6: run_linear / HCQGraph batch launch - DepsTracker sync - result in Buffer
Example: matmul+reshape+sum fuses to 1 kernel via laziness - DEBUG=4 prints generated source
TinyJit replays Steps 2-6 after first capture - skips Python overhead on hot path
Between PyTorch and micrograd - full stack you can read and hack in an afternoon
pip install -e . - python3 -c "from tinygrad import Tensor; Tensor.eye(3).realize()"
DEBUG=3 fusion trace - examples/beautiful_mnist.py 98% acc in ~5s - docs.tinygrad.org
Design Position (entire DL stack as UOp graph rewrites - simplicity over line-count golf)
Lazy fusion + pattern-matched lowering + BEAM kernel search + HCQ graphs = hackable end-to-end ML
Init: Tensor lazy build UOp DAG - realize() or TinyJit triggers schedule + compile + run_linear
Loop: PatternMatcher rewrites - BEAM opts - render - HCQ batch - DepsTracker sync - buffer result
Sources: github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad - docs.tinygrad.org/developer - README - DeepWiki system architecture
